name: Machine Hip Abduction
summary: A seated machine exercise that isolates the hip abductors by pushing the thighs outward against resistance.

setup: Sit back firmly against the backrest of the hip abduction machine.
Adjust the starting lever so the padded leg supports rest against the outside of your knees or thighs at an inward position that provides a comfortable stretch.
Place your feet flat on the footrests and hold the machine handles for stability.
steps: Press your thighs outward against the pads in a smooth, controlled motion.
Open your legs as wide as comfortably possible, contracting your outer hips and glutes at peak abduction.
Pause briefly at the end range of motion.
Slowly bring your legs back to the starting position without letting the weight stack slam.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you press your legs outward; inhale as you return to the start position.
cues: Push through the outer knees, not the feet
Keep your pelvis pinned to the seat

common_faults.fault: Using momentum or jerking the weight stack
common_faults.correction: Slow down the repetition tempo and pause briefly at peak contraction.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the lower back or hips off the seat pad
common_faults.correction: Grip the handles firmly and keep your glutes and lower back pressed against the seat.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the weight stack to slam between repetitions
common_faults.correction: Maintain muscular tension throughout the eccentric phase and reverse before the weights touch down.

precautions: Avoid setting the initial range of motion excessively narrow if it causes groin or hip impingement.
